selection_reasoning: These 4 tasks form a coherent survival scenario: The player must first find a jungle sign (which provides directional guidance to resources), then mine potatoes (a food-gathering prerequisite that requires finding the farm area), craft a stone sword (needed as a weapon to hunt rabbits), and finally craft cooked rabbit (which requires having killed a rabbit with the sword and cooking it). The dependency chain creates a multi-hop structure where exploration leads to resource gathering, which enables combat, which enables cooking. The jungle sign serves as a wayfinding element that directs the player toward the potato farm and crafting area. The stone sword is needed to efficiently kill a rabbit for the cooked rabbit recipe. Mining potatoes establishes the player is in the resource area where crafting stations are available.

edges.reason: The jungle sign provides directions to the potato farm area; player must read it to locate potatoes
The jungle sign indicates where crafting resources (cobblestone, sticks) and crafting table are located
Stone sword is needed to kill the rabbit, which drops raw rabbit required for cooking cooked_rabbit
Mining potatoes confirms player reached the resource area with the furnace needed to smelt raw rabbit into cooked rabbit

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The player must navigate near the jungle sign at spawn-relative (3, 0, 2) and face it to 'read' the directional text. max_distance=16 allows reading from a reasonable distance, and facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is looking toward the sign.

Uses inventory_has because mining fully-grown potato crops (age=7) drops potato items into the player's inventory. No potatoes exist in the starting inventory, so any potato in inventory confirms successful harvesting from the farm.

Uses inventory_has because crafting a stone sword (2 cobblestone + 1 stick on crafting table) places the result in the player's inventory. No stone sword exists in the scene initially, so its presence in inventory confirms successful crafting.

Uses inventory_has because smelting raw rabbit in the furnace with coal produces cooked_rabbit which the player picks up into inventory. No cooked rabbit exists in the scene initially (only raw rabbit in chest and on rabbits), so its presence confirms successful furnace smelting.

scene_description: A survival scenario centered around a jungle sign that provides directions. The sign points north to a potato farm and east to a crafting/smelting area. Two stationary rabbits are nearby for hunting. A chest with backup raw rabbit is near the crafting area. The player has cobblestone, sticks, and coal in inventory to craft a stone sword and cook rabbit.
task_text: Find and read the jungle sign for directions. Go north to mine potatoes from the farm. Use the crafting table to the east to craft a stone sword from cobblestone and sticks. Obtain raw rabbit (from killing a rabbit or the nearby chest), then smelt it in the furnace with coal to make cooked rabbit.
design_notes: Layout: Player spawns at origin. Jungle sign at ~3,0,2 (south-east, facing player, rotation=8 means facing south/toward spawn). Potato farm at ~-2 to ~2, z=-5 to -7 (north, 5-7 blocks away, 15 crops total). Crafting table at ~8,0,0 and furnace at ~8,0,2 (east, 8 blocks). Cobblestone wall at x=7 marks the crafting area visually. Two NoAI rabbits at ~3,0,-3 and ~4,0,-4 (between sign and farm, stationary for easy hunting). Chest with 2x raw_rabbit at ~9,0,1 near furnace as backup. Player starts with cobblestone(10), sticks(4), coal(5) for crafting stone sword and fueling furnace. All areas within 10 blocks of spawn, fully accessible on flat grass terrain.
